commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. 2	# Convert a PyBaMM expression tree to a CasADi expression tree
3	#
4	from __future__ import annotations
5	
6	import casadi
7	import numpy as np
8	from scipy import interpolate, special
9	
10	import pybamm
11	
12	
13	class CasadiConverter:
14	    def __init__(self, casadi_symbols=None):
15	        self._casadi_symbols = casadi_symbols or {}
16	
17	        pybamm.citations.register("Andersson2019")
18	
19	    def convert(
20	        self,
21	        symbol: pybamm.Symbol,
22	        t: casadi.MX,
23	        y: casadi.MX,
24	        y_dot: casadi.MX,
25	        inputs: dict | None,
26	    ) -> casadi.MX:
27	        """
28	        This function recurses down the tree, converting the PyBaMM expression tree to
29	        a CasADi expression tree
30	
31	        Parameters
32	        ----------
33	        symbol : :class:`pybamm.Symbol`
34	            The symbol to convert
35	        t : :class:`casadi.MX`
36	            A casadi symbol representing time
37	        y : :class:`casadi.MX`
38	            A casadi symbol representing state vectors
39	        y_dot : :class:`casadi.MX`
40	            A casadi symbol representing time derivatives of state vectors
41	        inputs : dict
42	            A dictionary of casadi symbols representing parameters
43	
44	        Returns
45	        -------
46	        :class:`casadi.MX`
47	            The converted symbol
48	        """
49	        try:
50	            return self._casadi_symbols[symbol]
51	        except KeyError:
52	            # Change inputs to empty dictionary if it's None
53	            inputs = inputs or {}
54	            casadi_symbol = self._convert(symbol, t, y, y_dot, inputs)
55	            self._casadi_symbols[symbol] = casadi_symbol
56	
57	            return casadi_symbol
58	
59	    def _convert(self, symbol, t, y, y_dot, inputs):
60	        """See :meth:`CasadiConverter.convert()`."""
61	        if isinstance(
62	            symbol,
63	            pybamm.Scalar | pybamm.Array | pybamm.Time | pybamm.InputParameter,
64	        ):
65	            return casadi.MX(symbol.evaluate(t, y, y_dot, inputs))
66	
67	        elif isinstance(symbol, pybamm.StateVector):
68	            if y is None:
69	                raise ValueError("Must provide a 'y' for converting state vectors")
70	            return casadi.vertcat(*[y[y_slice] for y_slice in symbol.y_slices])
71	
72	        elif isinstance(symbol, pybamm.StateVectorDot):
73	            if y_dot is None:
74	                raise ValueError("Must provide a 'y_dot' for converting state vectors")
75	            return casadi.vertcat(*[y_dot[y_slice] for y_slice in symbol.y_slices])
76	
77	        elif isinstance(symbol, pybamm.BinaryOperator):
78	            left, right = symbol.children
79	            # process children
80	            converted_left = self.convert(left, t, y, y_dot, inputs)
81	            converted_right = self.convert(right, t, y, y_dot, inputs)
82	
83	            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Modulo):
84	                return casadi.fmod(converted_left, converted_right)
85	            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Minimum):
86	                return casadi.fmin(converted_left, converted_right)
87	            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Maximum):
88	                return casadi.fmax(converted_left, converted_right)
89	
90	            # _binary_evaluate defined in derived classes for specific rules
91	            return symbol._binary_evaluate(converted_left, converted_right)
92	
93	        elif isinstance(symbol, pybamm.UnaryOperator):
94	            converted_child = self.convert(symbol.child, t, y, y_dot, inputs)
95	            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.AbsoluteValue):
96	                return casadi.fabs(converted_child)
97	            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Floor):
98	                return casadi.floor(converted_child)
99	            if isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Ceiling):
100	                return casadi.ceil(converted_child)
101	            return symbol._unary_evaluate(converted_child)
102	
103	        elif isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Function):
104	            converted_children = [
105	                self.convert(child, t, y, y_dot, inputs) for child in symbol.children
106	            ]
107	            # Special functions
108	            if symbol.function == np.min:
109	                return casadi.mmin(*converted_children)
110	            elif symbol.function == np.max:
111	                return casadi.mmax(*converted_children)
112	            elif symbol.function == np.abs:
113	                return casadi.fabs(*converted_children)
114	            elif symbol.function == np.sqrt:
115	                return casadi.sqrt(*converted_children)
116	            elif symbol.function == np.sin:
117	                return casadi.sin(*converted_children)
118	            elif symbol.function == np.arcsinh:
119	                return casadi.arcsinh(*converted_children)
120	            elif symbol.function == np.arccosh:
121	                return casadi.arccosh(*converted_children)
122	            elif symbol.function == np.tanh:
123	                return casadi.tanh(*converted_children)
124	            elif symbol.function == np.cosh:
125	                return casadi.cosh(*converted_children)
126	            elif symbol.function == np.sinh:
127	                return casadi.sinh(*converted_children)
128	            elif symbol.function == np.cos:
129	                return casadi.cos(*converted_children)
130	            elif symbol.function == np.exp:
131	                return casadi.exp(*converted_children)
132	            elif symbol.function == np.log:
133	                return casadi.log(*converted_children)
134	            elif symbol.function == np.sign:
135	                return casadi.sign(*converted_children)
136	            elif symbol.function == special.erf:
137	                return casadi.erf(*converted_children)
138	            elif isinstance(symbol, pybamm.Interpolant):
139	                if symbol.interpolator == "linear":
140	                    solver = "linear"
141	                elif symbol.interpolator == "cubic":
142	                    solver = "bspline"
143	                elif symbol.interpolator == "pchip":
144	                    x_np = np.array(symbol.x[0])
145	                    y_np = np.array(symbol.y)
146	                    pchip_interp = interpolate.PchipInterpolator(x_np, y_np)
147	                    d_np = pchip_interp.derivative()(x_np)
148	                    x = converted_children[0]
149	
150	                    def hermite_poly(i):
151	                        x0 = x_np[i]
152	                        x1 = x_np[i + 1]
153	                        h_val = x1 - x0
154	                        h_val_mx = casadi.MX(h_val)
155	                        y0 = casadi.MX(y_np[i])
156	                        y1 = casadi.MX(y_np[i + 1])
157	                        d0 = casadi.MX(d_np[i])
158	                        d1 = casadi.MX(d_np[i + 1])
159	                        xn = (x - x0) / h_val_mx
160	                        h00 = 2 * xn**3 - 3 * xn**2 + 1
161	                        h10 = xn**3 - 2 * xn**2 + xn
162	                        h01 = -2 * xn**3 + 3 * xn**2
163	                        h11 = xn**3 - xn**2
164	                        return (
165	                            h00 * y0
166	                            + h10 * h_val_mx * d0
167	                            + h01 * y1
168	                            + h11 * h_val_mx * d1
169	                        )
170	
171	                    # Build piecewise polynomial for points inside the domain.
172	                    inside = casadi.MX.zeros(x.shape)
173	                    for i in range(len(x_np) - 1):
174	                        cond = casadi.logic_and(x >= x_np[i], x <= x_np[i + 1])
175	                        inside = casadi.if_else(cond, hermite_poly(i), inside)
176	
177	                    # Extrapolation:
178	                    left = hermite_poly(0)  # For x < x_np[0]
179	                    right = hermite_poly(len(x_np) - 2)  # For x > x_np[-1]
180	
181	                    # if greater than the maximum, use right; otherwise, use the piecewise value.
182	                    result = casadi.if_else(
183	                        x < x_np[0], left, casadi.if_else(x > x_np[-1], right, inside)
184	                    )
185	                    return result
186	                else:  # pragma: no cover
187	                    raise NotImplementedError(
188	                        f"Unknown interpolator: {symbol.interpolator}"
189	                    )
190	
191	                if len(converted_children) == 1:
192	                    if solver == "linear":
193	                        test = casadi.MX.interpn_linear(
194	                            symbol.x, symbol.y.flatten(), converted_children
195	                        )
196	                        if test.shape[0] == 1 and test.shape[1] > 1:
197	                            # for some reason, pybamm.Interpolant always returns a column vector, so match that
198	                            test = test.T
199	                        return test
200	                    elif solver == "bspline":
201	                        bspline = interpolate.make_interp_spline(
202	                            symbol.x[0], symbol.y, k=3
203	                        )
204	                        knots = [bspline.t]
205	                        coeffs = bspline.c.flatten()
206	                        degree = [bspline.k]
207	                        m = len(coeffs) // len(symbol.x[0])

I wrote the answer to the output file: `["KeyError", "TypeError", "ValueError"]`. I got this by reading the code, since nothing can be run in this environment.

How each exception arises, from `src/pybamm/expression_tree/operations/convert_to_casadi.py` and `input_parameter.py`:

- **`KeyError`**:
  - `CasadiConverter.convert` first looks the symbol up in its cache. Every first lookup misses and raises a `KeyError`, which PyBaMM catches itself (line 51).
  - In test 7, the input parameter `u` is missing from `inputs`, so `InputParameter._base_evaluate` raises a `KeyError`. It passes up through the `_convert` frame and out of `to_casadi`.
- **`ValueError`**:
  - Test 3 passes no `y` for a `StateVector` (line 69).
  - Test 4 passes no `y_dot` for a `StateVectorDot` (line 74).
- **`TypeError`**:
  - Test 5 converts a `Variable`, which has no conversion branch (line 296).
  - In test 10, `grad(c)` converts its child `Variable` first. That child raises the same `TypeError` before `Gradient._unary_evaluate` is ever reached, so its `NotImplementedError` never happens.

Tests 1, 2, 6, 8 and 9 convert without errors, apart from the internal cache-miss `KeyError`s.
